title: Romper a: Breaking Into Sound and Tears

sections.content:
You know *empezar a*, *ponerse a* and *echarse a* + infinitive. *Romper a* + infinitive is a fourth way to say that something suddenly starts, and it has a special picture: the start breaks a silence or a calm. It is used with sounds and feelings that burst out, such as *llorar* (to cry), *reír* (to laugh), *gritar* (to shout), *aplaudir* (to applaud) and *llover* (to rain).

Unlike *echarse*, *romper* is not reflexive, so there is no *se*. You meet it mostly in stories and news reports, usually in the preterite.

sections.title: romper a + infinitive
rows: Al terminar el concierto, el público rompió a aplaudir.
When the concert ended, the audience burst into applause.
Después de un largo silencio, la niña rompió a llorar.
After a long silence, the girl burst into tears.
Cuando se abrieron las puertas, los niños rompieron a gritar de alegría.
When the doors opened, the children broke into shouts of joy.
Hacia la tarde, rompió a llover con fuerza.
Towards evening, it suddenly started to pour.

sections.content: Use *romper a* only with sounds, feelings and rain. For a planned task it is wrong (*Rompió a estudiar* does not exist), and for movement *echarse a correr* is the natural choice. Do not add *se*: *Se rompió a llorar* is not Spanish.
